reviews.title: Serious Build Quality Issue
reviews.comment:
I’ve had the exact same issue as others: the AIO LCD unit screws are prone to breaking. They seem to fail under the stress of normal heat expansion.
Before you install this, do the following:
1 Inspect the 4 Philips screws inside the LCD housing.
2 Ensure they are tightened properly.
3 Check for any gaps between the LCD screen and the plastic frame.
If anything looks loose, it’s a ticking time bomb. It’s a known issue that definitely needs a revision from the manufacturer.

reviews.title: Over Priced Mess
reviews.comment:
The base of the AIO is solid. The 420mm rad works great. RGB and screen is there this overpriced peice of hardware becomes trash.
The fans with the AIO are not the same as the SWAFANS they typically sell. These have a decent magnetic connection and are controlled via the motherboard. However you get a single cable for this so you cannot use the fans independently if you want.
The screen requires you use the Thermaltake control software and it is GARBAGE. It does not work right half the time and often I have to reboot the system to make the screen appear in the software.
This is way over priced for the quality of the software the screen being barely functional.
